```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                       fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 0.3)

# draws n full-width blank lines (margin to margin) for handwritten answers,
# as a single plot so spacing is deterministic; pair with fig.height = 0.3 * n
blank_lines <- function(n = 1) {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, n), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    segments(0, n - i + 0.5, 1, n - i + 0.5, lwd = 1)
  }
}

# reserves blank work space (no ruled lines); pair with fig.height
blank_space <- function() {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot.new()
}

# fill-in table drawn with base graphics so row height is controllable;
# body = list of rows, each a list/vector of cell strings ("" = blank)
blank_table <- function(headers, body, col_widths = NULL,
                        header_height = 0.35, row_height = 0.5,
                        cex = 0.95, bold_rows = integer(0), ans = NULL) {
  nc <- length(headers); nr <- length(body)
  if (is.null(col_widths)) col_widths <- rep(1, nc)
  col_widths <- col_widths / sum(col_widths)
  cx <- c(0, cumsum(col_widths))
  h_total <- header_height + nr * row_height
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0), family = "serif")
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, h_total), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "",
       xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")
  y <- h_total
  segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = 1.5)
  y <- y - header_height
  segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = 1.5)
  for (i in seq_len(nr)) {
    y <- y - row_height
    segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = if (i == nr) 1.5 else 0.5,
             col = if (i == nr) "black" else "grey70")
  }
  for (v in cx) segments(v, 0, v, h_total, lwd = 1)
  yh <- h_total - header_height / 2
  for (j in seq_len(nc)) text((cx[j] + cx[j + 1]) / 2, yh, labels = headers[[j]], font = 2, cex = cex)
  y <- h_total - header_height
  for (i in seq_len(nr)) {
    yc <- y - row_height / 2
    fnt <- if (i %in% bold_rows) 2 else 1
    for (j in seq_len(nc)) {
      val <- body[[i]][[j]]
      is_ans <- !is.null(ans) && isTRUE(ans[[i]][[j]])
      if (!identical(val, "")) text((cx[j] + cx[j + 1]) / 2, yc, labels = val,
                                    font = if (is_ans) 3 else fnt, cex = cex,
                                    col = if (is_ans) ans_col else "black")
    }
    y <- y - row_height
  }
}

# keeps a prompt and its answer space on one PDF page: place `r nq(...)` on its
# own line just above the prompt. Emits nothing in non-LaTeX output. lines =
# lines of prompt text, rows = rows of blank space below it (0.3 in each),
# extra = any other height (in inches), e.g. a figure or table
nq <- function(lines, rows = 0, extra = 0) {
  if (!knitr::is_latex_output()) return("")
  knitr::asis_output(sprintf("\n\\needspace{%.2fin}\n", 0.23 * lines + 0.15 + 0.3 * rows + extra))
}

ans_col <- rgb(200, 0, 130, maxColorValue = 255)
ponds <- read.csv("../../data/BdRegionalSurvey.csv")
covars <- c("water_temp_c", "elevation_m", "canopy_pct", "conductivity_us",
            "area_ha", "fish", "bullfrogs", "road_km")
X <- scale(as.matrix(ponds[, covars]))
colnames(X) <- c("temp", "elev", "canopy", "cond", "area", "fish", "bullfrogs", "road")
y_bin <- cbind(ponds$bd_positive, ponds$frogs_swabbed - ponds$bd_positive)

# candidate models: NLL at the MLE (rounded to 2 decimals, as printed)
fit_nll <- function(cols) {
  f <- if (length(cols) == 0) glm(y_bin ~ 1, family = binomial) else
    glm(y_bin ~ X[, cols, drop = FALSE], family = binomial)
  round(-as.numeric(logLik(f)), 2)
}
models <- list(character(0), "temp", "elev", c("temp", "elev"),
               c("temp", "bullfrogs", "canopy"),
               c("temp", "elev", "bullfrogs", "canopy"), colnames(X))
model_labels <- c("intercept only", "temp", "elevation", "temp + elevation",
                  "temp + bullfrogs + canopy", "temp + elev. + bullfrogs + canopy",
                  "all eight")
k <- sapply(models, length) + 1
nll <- sapply(models, fit_nll)
aic <- 2 * nll + 2 * k
f2 <- function(v) formatC(v, format = "f", digits = 2)

# NLL surface for the temp + elevation model, intercept profiled out
zt <- X[, "temp"]
ze <- X[, "elev"]
nll_2d <- function(bt, be) {
  eta_off <- bt * zt + be * ze
  f <- function(b0) -sum(dbinom(ponds$bd_positive, ponds$frogs_swabbed,
                                plogis(b0 + eta_off), log = TRUE))
  optimize(f, c(-4, 3))$objective
}
bt_grid <- seq(-0.8, 0.45, length.out = 101)
be_grid <- seq(-0.45, 0.8, length.out = 101)
nll_surf <- outer(bt_grid, be_grid, Vectorize(nll_2d))
mle_2d <- coef(glm(y_bin ~ zt + ze, family = binomial))[-1]

# answers: AIC from the printed (rounded) NLLs; LRTs; constrained estimates on each budget
d_aic <- aic - min(aic)
lrt_56 <- 2 * (nll[5] - nll[6])
lrt_57 <- 2 * (nll[5] - nll[7])
budget <- 0.4
theta <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 1441)
circle <- cbind(budget * cos(theta), budget * sin(theta))
s <- seq(-1, 1, length.out = 801)
diamond <- rbind(cbind(budget * s, budget * (1 - abs(s))), cbind(budget * s, -budget * (1 - abs(s))))
ridge_est <- circle[which.min(apply(circle, 1, function(b) nll_2d(b[1], b[2]))), ]
lasso_est <- diamond[which.min(apply(diamond, 1, function(b) nll_2d(b[1], b[2]))), ]
r_te <- cor(ponds$water_temp_c, ponds$elevation_m)
```

\ans{\textbf{Answer key.} Answers are in magenta sans-serif type; longer answers have a bar in the margin.}

## The scenario

The summer after the 12-pond survey from Lab 7, the field crew swabbed
frogs at **60 ponds** across the region and recorded eight features of
each pond: water temperature, elevation, canopy cover, conductivity,
pond area, whether fish are present, whether bullfrogs are present (an
invasive species that carries Bd without dying from it), and distance
to the nearest road. Managers can afford to monitor only some ponds and
want to know which features predict where Bd is common.

```{r scatter, fig.height=2.7}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(3.4, 3.8, 0.6, 0.6), mgp = c(2.1, 0.6, 0))
plot(ponds$water_temp_c, ponds$bd_positive / ponds$frogs_swabbed, pch = 19,
     col = ifelse(ponds$bullfrogs == 1, "black", "grey60"),
     xlab = "Water temperature (°C)", ylab = "Proportion Bd-positive")
legend("topright", c("bullfrogs", "no bullfrogs"), pch = 19,
       col = c("black", "grey60"), bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
plot(ponds$water_temp_c, ponds$elevation_m, pch = 19, col = "grey30",
     xlab = "Water temperature (°C)", ylab = "Elevation (m)")
legend("topright", paste0("r = ", f2(cor(ponds$water_temp_c, ponds$elevation_m))),
       bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
```

The model for every candidate is the logistic-binomial model from Lab 7,
with more predictors: the number of Bd-positive frogs at pond $i$ is
Binomial($n_i$, $p_i$), with
$$\text{logit}(p_i) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_{1i} + \beta_2 x_{2i} + \dots$$
Every predictor was **standardized** (mean 0, SD 1) before fitting, so
each $\beta$ is the change in log-odds of infection per standard
deviation of that predictor.

**Which pond features predict Bd prevalence?**

Please keep laptops closed for this Act.

`r nq(5, 0, extra = 4.2)`

## Part 1: Comparing candidate models (individual, ~20 min)

The table lists seven candidate models, the number of parameters $k$
(including $\beta_0$), and each model's negative log-likelihood (NLL)
at its MLE.

**1a.** Fill in the missing AIC values ($\text{AIC} = 2\,\text{NLL} + 2k$)
and every $\Delta$AIC.

```{r aic-table, fig.height=4.1}
rows <- lapply(seq_along(models), function(i) {
  c(as.character(i), model_labels[i], as.character(k[i]), f2(nll[i]), f2(aic[i]), f2(d_aic[i]))
})
ans_cells <- lapply(seq_along(models), function(i) {
  c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, !(i %in% c(1, 4, 6)), TRUE)
})
blank_table(c("Model", "Predictors", "k", "NLL", "AIC", "dAIC"), rows,
            col_widths = c(0.6, 2.9, 0.4, 0.9, 1, 1), row_height = 0.52, cex = 0.85,
            ans = ans_cells)
```

`r nq(4, 4)`

**1b.** Which model is best by AIC? Model 6 adds elevation to Model 5
and sits within 2 AIC units of it. Does that mean the data support an
effect of elevation? Use the NLLs.

\ansbegin

Model 5 (temp + bullfrogs + canopy), AIC `r f2(aic[5])`. No: adding
elevation lowers the NLL by only `r f2(nll[5] - nll[6])`. A parameter
with no effect at all costs at most 2 AIC units, so landing within 2 is
expected even if elevation does nothing.

\ansend

`r nq(6, 9)`

**1c.** Use likelihood ratio tests to compare Model 5 with Model 6, and
Model 5 with Model 7. For each, give the test statistic, its degrees of
freedom, and your conclusion. Critical values of $\chi^2$ at the 0.05
level: 3.84 (1 df), 5.99 (2), 7.81 (3), 9.49 (4), 11.07 (5).

\ansbegin

Model 5 vs. 6: $D = 2(`r f2(nll[5])` - `r f2(nll[6])`) = `r f2(lrt_56)`$,
1 df; $`r f2(lrt_56)` < 3.84$, so keep Model 5.

Model 5 vs. 7: $D = 2(`r f2(nll[5])` - `r f2(nll[7])`) = `r f2(lrt_57)`$,
5 df; $`r f2(lrt_57)` < 11.07$, so keep Model 5.

\ansend

`r nq(5, 5)`

**1d.** Models 2 and 3 are nearly tied. Can these data tell whether
water temperature or elevation is what drives Bd? Why or why not? What
kind of ponds, or what kind of study, would help?

\ansbegin

No. Temperature and elevation are strongly correlated
($r = `r f2(r_te)`$), so either one alone fits about equally well
($\Delta$AIC `r f2(abs(aic[2] - aic[3]))`). Helpful: ponds where the two
come apart (warm high ponds, cold low ponds, e.g. spring-fed or shaded
sites), or an experiment that changes water temperature directly.

\ansend

`r nq(10, 0, extra = 5)`

## Part 2: Penalties as budgets (individual, ~15 min)

A ridge penalty, $\text{NLL}(\beta) + \lambda \sum_j \beta_j^2$, gives
the same estimate as finding the lowest-NLL point inside a **budget**
$\sum_j \beta_j^2 \le t^2$, for some $t$ that shrinks as $\lambda$
grows. The lasso budget is $\sum_j |\beta_j| \le t$. Neither budget
includes $\beta_0$.

The figure shows NLL contours for Model 4 (temperature and elevation
only), labeled by how far each lies above the minimum. The $\times$
marks the MLE.

```{r contours, fig.width=5, fig.height=5}
par(mar = c(3.6, 3.8, 0.6, 0.6), mgp = c(2.2, 0.6, 0))
plot(NA, xlim = range(bt_grid), ylim = range(be_grid), asp = 1, xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i",
     xlab = "Temperature coefficient", ylab = "Elevation coefficient")
abline(v = seq(-0.8, 0.4, 0.1), h = seq(-0.4, 0.8, 0.1), col = "grey90")
abline(v = 0, h = 0, col = "grey40", lwd = 1.5)
contour(bt_grid, be_grid, nll_surf - min(nll_surf),
        levels = c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16),
        add = TRUE, labcex = 0.65, col = "grey20")
points(mle_2d[1], mle_2d[2], pch = 4, cex = 1.6, lwd = 2.5)
lines(circle, col = ans_col, lwd = 2, lty = 2)
polygon(rbind(c(budget, 0), c(0, budget), c(-budget, 0), c(0, -budget)),
        border = ans_col, lwd = 2)
points(rbind(ridge_est, lasso_est), pch = c(21, 24), bg = ans_col, cex = 1.5)
legend("bottomright", c("ridge budget (circle)", "lasso budget (diamond)",
                        "ridge estimate", "lasso estimate"),
       col = ans_col, lty = c(2, 1, NA, NA), lwd = 2, pch = c(NA, NA, 21, 24),
       pt.bg = ans_col, bty = "o", bg = "white", cex = 0.75, text.col = ans_col)
box()
```

`r nq(4, 2)`

**2a.** On the figure, draw the ridge budget
$\beta_{temp}^2 + \beta_{elev}^2 \le 0.4^2$ and the lasso budget
$|\beta_{temp}| + |\beta_{elev}| \le 0.4$. Mark the ridge estimate and
the lasso estimate, and read off their approximate coordinates.

Ridge: \ans{(`r f2(ridge_est[1])`, `r f2(ridge_est[2])`)}   Lasso:
\ans{(`r f2(lasso_est[1])`, `r f2(lasso_est[2])`)} \ans{(approximate
values from a sketch are fine)}

`r nq(3, 4)`

**2b.** Did the lasso set either coefficient to exactly 0? Use the
shapes in your sketch to explain why or why not.

\ansbegin

No. The contours are long ellipses that run parallel to the diamond's
upper-left edge, so the lowest contour touches that edge partway along
it, not at a corner. Both coefficients stay nonzero.

\ansend

`r nq(2, 4)`

**2c.** What would the contours have to look like for the lasso to set
the elevation coefficient to 0?

\ansbegin

The lowest contour would have to touch the diamond first at its corner
on the temperature axis, $(-0.4, 0)$: for example, rounder contours (if
temperature and elevation weren't correlated) centered near the
temperature axis (a small elevation effect), or ellipses tilted across
the edge rather than along it.

\ansend

`r nq(4, 6)`
